messages:
jen: Heads-up — the new python quickstart sample is leaking raw transport errors to users. Saw a user paste this into #support: 

jen: "Unhandled exception: HTTP 401 - b'Unauthorized', Traceback (most recent call last): ..."

nathan: Ugh. Is that from the SDK or our example app wrapper?

jen: From the sample app's main loop. We catch Exception and re-raise without mapping. The SDK actually does have typed exceptions (AuthError / RateLimitError) but sample app prints repr(e).

sam: That's a pretty bad first impression for new signups. We should catch and render friendly messages in the quickstart UI AND update example code to show recommended handling.

alex: Agree. Proposed small changes:
- Use sdk.exceptions.* in examples
- Show one-liner user-facing messages (no trace)
- Include snippet for backoff / retry hints for 429 and 5xx

maria: +1. Can we standardize the public error shape so apps can map easily? Right now HTTP 502 vs SDK ServerError vs generic Exception is inconsistent across languages.

nathan: We have an internal mapping but parity across SDKs is flaky. JS maps 401 -> AuthenticationError, py maps too but some wrappers rewrap it. Maybe expand docs and add a minimal typed error contract in the quickstart: what fields to expect (type, code, retry_after, user_message).

sam: Example for proposed error contract (showing python SDK):
```json
{
  "type": "AuthenticationError",
  "code": "AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN",
  "http_status": 401,
  "retryable": false,
  "user_message": "Your API key is invalid or expired. Re-authenticate at https://app.redwood.com/settings/api-keys"
}
```

jen: Love that. Two delivery asks: 1) patch quickstart samples (py + js) to surface user_message only, with a collapsible dev debug section for full error; 2) create a short doc page: "Error shapes & recommended handling" with mapping table and snippets for common cases.

alex: I can take the sample app patches (small PR). Will include a pattern for printing developer debug info behind ENV=DEV.

maria: I'll draft the doc page. Should include explicit guidance on when to retry vs when to surface to user (e.g., 429: ephemeral retry with backoff + inform user if persistent; 401: no retry).

nathan: Also add a tiny test harness in our sample app repo that simulates error responses so folks can see UX.

deploy-bot: deployment queued for branch "quickstart-errors-fix" by alex — ETA ~10m :rocket:

jen: Thanks all. Can we land the doc before EOD? It'll be handy for support and onboarding ops.

alex: I'll open the PR now and tag reviewers.

maria: Drafting the doc now, will drop a link in this thread when ready.

sam: After we ship, can we run a short experiment: new onboarding flow vs old and measure support ticket rate + time-to-first-success? If error UX helps, we can prioritize more examples.

jen: Good idea — labelling it as "onboarding-ux" experiment. I'll coordinate with growth for tracking.

nathan: Nice. Small follow-up: add a note in SDK changelog that we aim for parity on typed exceptions and the public error contract. That helps downstream libs.

jen: Perfect. Closing loop — thanks team :heart:
